One cross-lens conflict resolved: the architecture lens claimed zoho-bigin's `appConfig` import is now unused — it isn't (still used at lines 12 and 22). The other three lenses had it right, so I'm reporting that finding as de-parameterization/self-inconsistency, not an unused import.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update()` called but `prisma` is never imported (imports end line 20; sole occurrence of the identifier). TS2304 + runtime ReferenceError on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, since getClient() is invoked unconditionally from the constructor at line 57. Independently verified.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse envelope, not `.data`; `data: { key }` persists `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` into Credential.key. Next load, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75, outside the try/catch) throws — permanent Google Calendar credential corruption on the first refresh, sync enabled or not. Typechecks because Prisma's key field is InputJsonValue.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59 — the `state?.teamId` branch returns at line 56, before `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` at line 59; line 59 is therefore only reachable with `teamId: null` and is dead code. The sole guard on team-credential creation is `members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }` — any accepted MEMBER, no role check. A plain member can pass `state={"teamId":<victimTeam>}` through the OAuth redirect and install a team-wide Stripe/HubSpot/Salesforce/MS Teams/Webex credential they control.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with no non-empty assertion. Secret unset + header omitted → `undefined !== undefined` is false → authenticated. `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` (the shipped .env.example value) + empty header → same bypass.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-92 — caller-supplied `userId`/`appSlug`/`keys` are written verbatim to Credential.key with no tenant scoping and no per-app schema validation; the update branch overwrites an existing legitimate credential in place. One leaked secret = attacker-controlled OAuth tokens substituted onto any user's calendar integration, no re-consent, no UI change.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal `"[object Object]"`; the second overwrites the first. Effective schema is `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}`. The "any numeric property is the expiry" comment describes behavior that does not exist, and z.object strips unknowns, so in sync mode every field except access_token is discarded. Verified empirically by two lenses against zod 3.25.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` persists a literal placeholder into a secret field. Because of the schema bug above it fires on every sync refresh; office365calendar:264 spreads it over the real refresh token before the DB write. Also regresses the non-sync path: previously an absent refresh_token left the stored one intact. Recovery requires full re-consent.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19 — `refreshFunction: () => any` collapses the return union to `any`, so the sync branch (raw fetch Response) and the fallback branch (Gaxios response / SDK object / Response) are structurally different types that TypeScript cannot distinguish. This is the single root cause of the six per-app defects below. A normalizing wrapper returning `{access_token, refresh_token?, expires_in?}` with a per-app mapper callback is the correct shape.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-96 — sync branch returns a Response; `res?.data` is undefined; `token.access_token` throws TypeError; the catch at 103 swallows it (message !== "invalid_grant") and returns stale expired auth. Google Calendar silently never refreshes under sync.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-202 — a Response is annotated `HubspotToken`; `expiresIn` undefined → `expiryDate` NaN; the Response object is written as the credential key (serializes to `{}`); `setAccessToken(undefined)`. Swallowed by the catch at 203. HubSpot credential wiped silently. HubSpot also never calls parseRefreshTokenResponse, so nothing maps snake_case → camelCase.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95 — sync response lacks Lark's `{code,msg,data}` envelope, so `data.data.refresh_token` is undefined and expiry fields become NaN. On the next call `!refreshToken` is true and line 62 runs `prisma.credential.delete` — silent credential destruction.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:84-95 — writes `key: responseBody` wholesale, replacing the entire credential. Under sync the response has no refresh_token, so it is deleted from the stored key permanently; getToken at 104 then calls refreshAccessToken(undefined). Unrecoverable if sync is later disabled.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:62-91 — wired into refreshOAuthTokens but still validates with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires refresh_token, refresh_token_expires_in, token_type literal and an exact scope literal. A sync response can never satisfy it → always "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Webex is advertised as synced but cannot work.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-281 — under sync, minimumTokenResponseSchema strips expires_in and applies no transform, so `isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)` stays true forever: every Office 365 calendar operation re-hits the sync endpoint. Self-inflicted request amplification.
Four of six migrated apps (hubspot, larkcalendar, office365video, webex) got refreshOAuthTokens without parseRefreshTokenResponse — the abstraction was applied half-way.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — the outbound sync POST carries no shared secret, HMAC, or bearer token, even though the inbound webhook is secret-gated. Anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can mint tokens for an arbitrary calcomUserId. No `response.ok` check (a 5xx/HTML page is handed to each parser as a token payload), no timeout/AbortSignal (a hung endpoint blocks all calendar ops), no TLS enforcement (an http:// value ships tokens in cleartext).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — the `&& userId` guard silently excludes all team credentials (userId null) from sync — the very credentials createOAuthAppCredential creates in this same change. No log, no warning; the sync payload has no teamId field at all.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-90 — findFirst-then-create is a non-atomic check-then-act with no transaction and no idempotency key. The author's own comment ("Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id") is proof no @@unique([userId, appId]) exists. Concurrent/retried deliveries create duplicate credential rows; out-of-order delivery overwrites a newer key with an older one.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-70 — `findFirst` with no orderBy is nondeterministic once duplicates exist, and an UPDATE physically relocates the row, so successive syncs can ping-pong between two rows holding different key generations.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34 — `prisma.user.findUnique({where:{id}})` with no `select`, used only for an `if (!user)` existence check: pulls every User scalar (password, twoFactorSecret, identityProviderId, metadata) into memory on an externally-reachable endpoint. Should be `select: { id: true }`.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40-50 — the App lookup selects back the slug it was queried by, then indexes the static compile-time appStoreMetadata map with it. The round trip adds only "a row exists" and doesn't check `enabled`, so it isn't an install gate either.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31,57-59 — `schema.parse` (not safeParse), `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` are all unguarded; no try/catch anywhere in the handler. Malformed body, wrong key, or bad plaintext → unhandled 500 with a stack rather than a 4xx.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no `req.method` guard; GET/PUT/DELETE/PATCH all reach the mutation path.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:9-15,62-91 — the webhook is user-only (schema accepts only userId), so team credentials created by createOAuthAppCredential can never be synced. Half the feature has no counterpart in the other half.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-92 — no delete/revoke path. When the parent app revokes access, the Cal.com credential stays live forever — the "sync" is inbound create/update only.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73-80 — the update sets only `key` and never clears the `invalid` flag, so a credential previously marked invalid (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:112-117) stays permanently invalid even after fresh keys arrive.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27 — non-constant-time secret comparison (CWE-208); use crypto.timingSafeEqual on length-checked buffers.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used as a lookup key against Node's lowercased req.headers with no `.toLowerCase()`. .env.example only *comments* "Should be in lowercase". A mixed-case value makes the lookup always undefined — fail-closed only while the secret is non-empty, fail-open in combination with the bypass above.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:36-47,81,91 — distinct "User not found" vs "App not found" 404s and distinct created/updated messages echoing userId form a user/app enumeration oracle; minor post-auth, an unauthenticated primitive when combined with the secret bypass.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 — `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` lets the feature run with no encryption key, producing an opaque "Invalid key length" 500 rather than a startup config failure. Validate presence/length at module load.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-108 — an unconditional token refresh + prisma write was added to getClient (called eagerly from the constructor at line 57), with no expiry check. Every availability lookup and booking-page render burns a rate-limited Salesforce refresh grant plus a row write on the hot path, with no optimistic-concurrency guard.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101-108 — the refreshed token is then discarded: the jsforce.Connection is still built from the pre-refresh `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url` read at line 73. Pure cost, no benefit.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce is the one refreshing app in this change NOT routed through refreshOAuthTokens, so it silently does not participate in credential sync, while still importing parseRefreshTokenResponse (whose sync branch it can never reach).

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `response.statusText !== "OK"` is not a valid success check: HTTP/2 has no reason phrase and undici returns "". Throws on success, and throws with an empty message on a 400 invalid_grant. Use `!response.ok`. Propagating raw upstream statusText into a client-visible HttpError also leaks upstream detail.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-84 — host hardcoded to login.salesforce.com, so sandbox (test.salesforce.com) tenants post their consumer_secret and refresh token to the wrong host.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96-99 — `key: {...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token}` replaces the whole key with only salesforceTokenSchema's 7 fields; anything else previously on the key is dropped (and under sync, instance_url is stripped too).

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94 and packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — dead branches: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, so `.success` can never be false at these call sites.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-263 — the deleted console.error removed the only diagnostic (zod issues + raw MS body) for token-schema drift, and the replacement throws a bare Error with no cause. Old behavior logged and continued with existing credentials; new behavior is a hard failure. Unannounced control-flow change. (Counterpoint from the security lens: that log was writing raw MS access/refresh tokens to the server log, so removing it is a genuine improvement — the fix is a redacted log, not no log.)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 vs decodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 — near-identical files; encodeOAuthState is a JSON.parse→JSON.stringify identity round trip that encodes nothing, while all seven add.ts callers splice its result straight into an OAuth authorize URL where raw JSON braces/quotes need URI (ideally base64url) encoding.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — unguarded JSON.parse of the attacker-round-trippable `state` query param, with no schema validation. Reachable pre-authentication (googlecalendar/api/callback.ts:17 calls it before the session check at line 23) → SyntaxError → 500. Confirmed NOT exploitable as Prisma filter injection (a non-integer teamId is rejected by Prisma), but should be try/catch + zod validated.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `members: { select: { userId: true } }` is fetched and never read; materializes every member row per OAuth callback. `select: { id: true }` suffices.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:45,47-54,61-68 — team branch throws a bare Error (500) while the auth failure at line 25 uses HttpError(401); both branches use unguarded `create`, so a re-run OAuth callback accumulates duplicate credentials.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:13-14 — JSDoc says both `appData.type` and `appData.appId` are "the app slug", but callers pass a type for `type` (e.g. {appId:"msteams", type:"office365_video"}). Line 13 should read "the app type".

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — appSlug is a bare untyped string at six call sites with no binding to appStoreMetadata keys. All six strings verified correct today ("google-calendar", "hubspot", "lark-calendar", "office365-calendar", "msteams", "webex"), but a typo silently degrades an app to "never refreshes" with no type error and no log. Should be a union/enum or appConfig.slug.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `${appConfig.slug}` replaced with a hardcoded "zoho-bigin" while appConfig is still used at lines 12 and 22, leaving the file self-inconsistent and decoupling the redirect URI from the declared slug. Unrelated to credential sync, and it deletes the one call site that had the right pattern. Also now a template literal with no interpolation.

.env.example:+10-12 — "must be 32 bytes for AES256" paired with `openssl rand -base64 24` yields a 32-character key carrying 192 bits of entropy, and is inconsistent with the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET line four rows above which says -base64 32. Low severity: the length is correct for a utf8-keyed aes256 cipher, so this is an entropy/consistency nit, not a breakage. (Intent-preservation lens judged this a non-finding; recording it at low.)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6 — `import { decodeOAuthState } from "../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` from a file already inside _utils/oauth/; should be "./decodeOAuthState". Harmless, but evidence the 21-call-site relocation was a find/replace rather than a reviewed refactor.

Zero tests added. Five new unit-testable modules (parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens, decodeOAuthState, encodeOAuthState, createOAuthAppCredential) plus a new public API route, no *.test.ts / *.spec.ts / __tests__ anywhere in the diff.

.env.example:233-244 — four env-var comments are the only documentation for the feature. No spec for the sync endpoint's request/response contract (the authoritative source is an inline comment at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6-7), no encryption-format doc, no doc for the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED switch.

The ~21-call-site import relocation (_utils/* → _utils/oauth/*, zero behavior) is bundled with the feature. Four of those same files also changed refresh semantics, parser return types, persisted credential shape, and an authorization guard — changes that read as one-line import diffs at a glance.

packages/app-store/stripepayment/api/callback.ts:50-51 and packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:98 — PRE-EXISTING (verified present at HEAD~1), not introduced: `returnTo` from the state param is redirected to without getSafeRedirectUrl, unlike google:78/hubspot:54/salesforce:49/o365calendar:79/o365video:100. Since this change consolidates all of these onto shared _utils/oauth/ helpers, it's the natural moment to fix.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:151 — PRE-EXISTING, unchanged by this diff but in a touched file: `console.log("result of accessToken in fetchWebexApi", accessToken)` logs a live access token.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16 — stray empty `/** */` JSDoc block above the handler.
Two things constrain confidence, and I'd rather flag them than let them read as verified:

The checkout is a 30-file sparse fixture** — only diff-touched files exist. `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `packages/lib/crypto.ts`, `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, `appStoreMetaData`, `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam.ts`, and every app `config.json` are absent. So these remain **unverified**: whether `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is actually defined and what gates it (this determines the reachability of the webhook auth bypass); whether `symmetricDecrypt` uses authenticated AES-GCM or malleable CBC (a padding-oracle question over stored OAuth credentials); whether `Credential` has a `@@unique([userId, appId])`; and whether `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by slug or by dirName — the feasibility lens flagged that upstream Cal.com keys it by dirName, which would make `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` 404 for exactly the hyphenated slugs this change wires up. That one is worth checking first against the full tree.

The three highest-severity findings I verified myself rather than relying on a lens: `prisma` missing from the Salesforce imports, the Google Calendar safeParse-envelope write, and the unreachable admin check in `createOAuthAppCredential`. All three are confirmed from code present in the tree.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
